messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: Question about dpriors()
parts:
Dear all,

I am running the following spline growth model,

BayesSpline.model <- '
i =~ 1*BSMMAT0199sm + 1*BSMMAT0103sm + 1*BSMMAT0107sm + 1*BSMMAT0111sm + 1*BSMMAT0115sm
s1 =~ -2*BSMMAT0199sm + -1*BSMMAT0103sm + 0*BSMMAT0107sm + 0*BSMMAT0111sm + 0*BSMMAT0115sm 
s2 =~ 0*BSMMAT0199sm + 0*BSMMAT0103sm + 3*BSMMAT0107sm + 4*BSMMAT0111sm + 5*BSMMAT0115sm 
i~~0*s1
i~~0*s2
s1~~0*s2
'
fitG8Mathbl <- bgrowth(BayesSpline.model,data=timssG8imp,burnin=5000,sample=100000,dp=dpriors(alpha ="dunif(300,400)"))
summary(fitG8Mathbl)

I need to provide a distribution for the intercept i, and so I used dp=dpriors() and specified a more informative prior on what I believe is the correct specification of the latent mean in GCM.  I am receiving the following error message.

Error : The following error occured when compiling and adapting the model using rjags:
 Error in rjags::jags.model(model, data = dataenv, inits = inits, n.chains = length(runjags.object$end.state),  : 
  Error in node alpha[3,1,1]
Node inconsistent with parents



It may help to use failed.jags(c('model','data','inits')) to see model/data/inits syntax with line numbers
Error in blavaan(BayesSpline.model, data = timssG8imp, dp = dpriors(alpha = "dunif(300,400)"),  : 
  blavaan ERROR: problem with MCMC estimation.  The model syntax and data have been exported.


Any thoughts would be helpful

Thanks,

David

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Question about dpriors()
parts:
David,

I am guessing this happens because the starting value of alpha will be closer to 0, outside of the (300,400) bounds. Then jags chokes because the starting value of "alpha" is inconsistent with the prior. If you used a normal prior with almost all its density in (300,400), I guess it might work. Here are a couple other possibilities for getting it to work with the uniform prior (from easier to harder; hopefully easier works...):

1. Try the argument inits="prior".

2. lavaan has a start() modified that can be used in the model syntax, which might help you here (but there is a chance that it doesn't work in blavaan, I can't immediately remember).

3. Section 3.4 of the blavaan paper (URL below, should be appearing in J Statistical Software soon) provides some info on setting custom initial values "by hand".

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604.pdf

Ed
